Git history plus the daily Drive tgz is the backup for every tracked config file. Never leave a .bak copy beside the file; commit before a risky edit.

Every record home (handoffs, audits, status, memory) is a search root, so a record can always be found where it was written.
Tool source lives in a git repo. ~/.claude holds installed copies or links, and STORAGE.md names the source of each one.
Retired things leave the live tree the day they retire: projects go to ~/DEV/_ARCHIVE, drained copies to ~/_PARKED_COPIES, proven clutter to ~/.Trash/<name>-<date>.

The memory-write tier rules are clear, but four mechanisms keep creating second copies: (1) dev-sync/mirror_memory.py keeps a Windows twin of every Tier A folder; 11 pairs are byte-identical and the main ~/DEV pair is 23 files apart; memsearch still indexes 3 C--Users twins while recall.py picks the newest copy; (2) 8 Mac Tier A folders were made with '_' in the slug, but Claude Code 2.1.308 folds '_' to '-'. No session has ever loaded them, and memory-write SKILL.md:105 and remember.py still steer new writes into them; (3) harvest-dev-docs never prunes, so 43 of the 158 dev-docs folders are for archived or gone repos, and one is a copy of Linda_Projects' STATUS that ends up in the indexes; (4) a second global-memory clone at ~/DEV/claude-global-memory, 26 commits behind, is the copy of the global-memory STATUS that the indexes see.
